issues.legal_issue: A revisional authority cannot cancel a quasi-permanent allotment of rural evacuee property when the original authority was barred from cancelling it.
material_facts: The disputed land was rural evacuee property allotted on a quasi-permanent basis.
The cancellation was sought after the rule restricting cancellation had come into force, and the circumstances did not fall within its specified exceptions.
The Custodian dismissed the application, but the Custodian General cancelled the allotment in revision.
issues.conclusion: The Custodian General lacked power to cancel the allotment in revision, and the orders cancelling it were quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, the Custodian’s powers are subject to rules made under the Act; section 56(2)(i) authorizes rules prescribing the circumstances in which allotments may be cancelled. Amended rule 14(6) limits cancellation of quasi-permanent rural allotments to specified circumstances, and the restriction applies to cancellations after its commencement even where the allotment was made after that date. Under section 27, the Custodian General may examine the legality and propriety of an order but cannot do what the Custodian was prohibited from doing. The amendment also removed any inherent power to cancel an allotment for restitution outside the specified circumstances.

predicates.quasi_permanent_rural_allotment: The authority allotted evacuee rural land to a person on a quasi-permanent basis.
predicates.cancellation_after_restriction_takes_eff: The authority sought to cancel the allotment after a rule restricting cancellation had taken effect.
predicates.revision_review_of_custodian_order: A higher authority considered the Custodian’s order in revision.
predicates.cancellation_ground_outside_permitted_ci: The proposed cancellation was based on a ground not among the circumstances in which the governing rule permitted cancellation.

issues.definition: When a higher authority reviews a Custodian’s order concerning a quasi-permanent rural allotment and the proposed post-restriction cancellation falls outside the permitted circumstances, the cancellation is without authority.

issues.legal_issue: A party’s new challenge to the validity of an allotment is not considered when that ground was not raised in its statement of case.
material_facts: The respondents argued that the appellants’ allotment was itself invalid because an earlier cancellation had contravened the governing rule.
The respondents had not raised that ground in their statement of case, so the appellants had not been given the opportunity to answer it.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to consider the new ground.
issues.legal_principle: A new ground not raised in the statement of case need not be considered where the opposing party was not given the opportunity to answer it.

predicates.supreme_court_appeal: The matter is before the Supreme Court on appeal.
predicates.challenge_ground_not_raised_in_statement: A party advances a challenge ground that it did not raise in its statement of case.
predicates.opposing_party_lacked_opportunity_to_ans: The opposing party was not given an opportunity to provide an answer to that ground.

issues.definition: In an appeal, when a party advances a ground absent from its statement of case and the opposing party had no opportunity to answer it, the Court declines to consider that ground.
